title: Backup control-plane orchestration and provenance

source_evidence.summary: Bahia should manage backup orchestration and provenance as a backup control plane, not implement deduplicated storage, block snapshotting, repository formats, or delta algorithms.

Bahia backup control-plane patterns now include kind 38400 backup-run intake plus restore request/approval kinds 38402/38403 and retention enforcement kind 38404 through the existing Nostr reactor validation, dedupe, authorization, EOSE, CLOSED, and AUTH path. Responders publish signed status/result events with per-relay summaries, and the projector emits BackupRestoreState 31998.

docs/control-planes.md now allocates backup-specific kinds 38400-38419, 6981-6984, 31991-31999, and 31310-31311. The allocation avoids existing artifact attestation kind 31200 and AI/ML result kinds 38395/38396.

Bahia now has a first-class BackupDefinition domain model and durable backup_definitions registry table/repository CRUD layer composing repository, policy, recipe, scheduling metadata, tenant/environment/owner scope, approval policy, restore target rules, executor targeting fields, labels/grouping, and audit fields.

Backup operational read models now persist and project first-class verification mode, evidence details, restore eligibility state/reason, verification policy failures, structured restore approval queue/audit reason fields, retention outcomes, failure categories, and fleet runtime posture summaries.

description: Bahia orchestrates backup policies, recipes, snapshot coordination, retention, provenance, restore workflows, verification/testing, cross-site replication, airgap export/import, and Nostr-signed backup attestations. Existing backup and snapshot tools own repository formats, deduplication, data transfer, compression, encryption primitives, and native snapshot implementation.

namespace_contract.collision_review: No collisions were found in the searched repository for the allocated backup kinds outside this planning/export material. The allocation intentionally avoids 31200, 38395, and 38396.
required_command_tags: p when routing to a specific agent or service
t or task where workflow correlation is needed
target where a protected resource is addressed
run where durable state already exists
required_result_tags: same relevant scoped tags as the command
run=<backup-run-id> when durable run state exists
namespace_contract.idempotency: Command processors deduplicate by event id and by the addressable coordinate (kind, pubkey, d-tag). Results use d=result:<request_event_id> and reply tags for correlation.

in_scope: Backup definitions, policies, recipes, runs, restore requests, restore results, verification records, retention policies, repository records, runtime statuses, observations, and signed attestations represented as Nostr events/read models.
Recipe-driven orchestration over runtime adapters such as Kopia, Velero, ZFS, Btrfs, LVM, Ceph, CSI, Longhorn, Proxmox, Restic, and Borg.
Verification-first backup workflows including hash verification, restore tests, service startup checks, health checks, boot checks, container checks, and model inference checks where applicable.

Scoped Nostr subscriptions, EOSE-driven historical catch-up, realtime event handling, publish OK verification, CLOSED handling, AUTH handling when required, event validation, dedupe, and idempotent handlers.
Portable backup recipes and signed operational provenance that connect deployments, artifacts, models, recipes, packages, SBOMs, backups, verification results, and restore outcomes.
out_of_scope: Replacing Kopia, Restic, Velero, Borg, ZFS, Btrfs, LVM, Ceph, CSI, Longhorn, or Proxmox backup/snapshot capabilities.
Polling relays or using timeout-based completion to detect backup or restore completion.

Changing the allocated backup namespace; retention execution outcomes are projected through the existing BackupRetentionRegistry 31994 and fleet posture through BackupRuntimeObservationState 31999 rather than adding new kind numbers.
preconditions: Operators configure relay, signer, and backend adapter credentials outside production code paths.
Runtime adapters expose backend capabilities and health without hardcoded production endpoints.
Backup recipes use narrow resource identifiers and correlation tags for relay filtering.
Implementation slices consume the allocated backup namespace from docs/control-planes.md rather than reusing 31200, 38395, or 38396.
postconditions: Every backup run has signed provenance describing initiator, target, backend, repository, artifact hashes or backend snapshot identifiers, verification mode/status/evidence details, explicit restore eligibility state, verification policy failures, and restore-test status when applicable.
Every publish path verifies relay OK accepted flag and rejection message.

Implemented backup, restore, and retention workflows are traceable from request through durable state, adapter execution, verification where required, signed status/result publication, and per-relay publish summaries.
Remaining implementation gaps are tracked in Beads rather than TODOs or markdown-only lists.
Authoritative backup definitions persist composed operator intent before command handlers, MCP, UI, scheduling dispatch, or executor placement are implemented.

Backup fleet posture is projected as Nostr read-model state including last successful run, last verification, last restore outcome, retention outcomes, backend health failures, queued/running/stale counts, pending approvals, and structured failure categories.
happy_paths: Operator defines a Kopia-backed filesystem backup recipe with retention and verification requirements; Bahia schedules or accepts a run request, orchestrates adapter execution, verifies results, and publishes signed run and verification events.

Operator requests a Kubernetes restore through a Velero adapter; Bahia validates request scope, records approval, orchestrates Velero, verifies restore health, and publishes signed restore result provenance.
A worker reconnects after relay interruption; Bahia re-issues scoped subscriptions and deduplicates replayed backup command/read-model events by event id and addressable d-tag coordinates.
failure_paths: Relay rejects a backup event publish; Bahia records failure with rejection reason and does not treat the workflow as complete.
Relay requires AUTH; Bahia completes NIP-42 authentication where configured or fails closed with an explicit result.
Backend adapter reports partial failure; Bahia records which backend operations succeeded, which failed, and what verification did or did not run.
Verification fails after snapshot creation; Bahia marks backup unverified and prevents policy consumers from treating it as a verified backup.
edge_cases: Batch publish partially succeeds across relays.
Duplicate run requests share the same idempotency d tag.
Historical catch-up returns older replaceable repository or policy events before the latest event.
Restore request targets an airgapped repository import that must be verified before use.
Backend supports snapshots but not application-aware quiesce/resume steps.
non_functional_requirements: Nostr-native event stream semantics only: subscribe, react, validate, verify, and close subscriptions cleanly.
No fake, stubbed, placeholder, filesystem_mock, or hardcoded production-path backup implementations in shipped backup orchestration paths.
Adapters must keep orchestration, storage, snapshot format, and artifact provenance decoupled.
Tests must be deterministic and inject EVENT, EOSE, OK, CLOSED, and AUTH messages directly rather than sleeping.
dependencies: Nostr event validation and publishing utilities
Backend-specific CLIs or APIs for Kopia, Velero, and native snapshot systems

resolved_ambiguities.question: Which event namespace should backup command/result and replaceable read-model events use?
resolved_ambiguities.decision: Use backup-specific command/result kinds 38400-38419, status/observation kinds 6981-6984, read models 31991-31999, and attestations 31310-31311.
resolved_ambiguities.evidence: docs/control-planes.md documents the allocation and collision rationale. Repository search found no current production collision for these allocated backup kinds.

resolved_ambiguities.question: Which production backend should the first vertical slice use?
resolved_ambiguities.decision: Use Kopia for the first filesystem backup-run slice. Bahia remains the control plane and delegates snapshot/verification execution to the real Kopia CLI adapter or explicit configuration/unsupported errors.
resolved_ambiguities.evidence: internal/adapters/backup/kopia_backend.go, internal/service/backup_run_coordinator.go, and related tests implement and verify the first Kopia-backed backup-run path.

resolved_ambiguities.question: When is a first-slice backup run restore-eligible?
resolved_ambiguities.decision: Restore eligibility is a first-class persisted state, not only an inferred boolean: eligible, run_not_succeeded, snapshot_missing, verification_pending, verification_failed, verification_skipped, verification_unsupported, policy_blocked, or unknown with an operator-facing reason.
resolved_ambiguities.evidence: domain.BackupRunRestoreEligibility/RestoreEligibility, backup run persistence/migration fields, registry/coordinator updates, and BackupRunState projection expose restore_eligibility and restore_eligibility_reason alongside verification mode/status.

resolved_ambiguities.question: How should the first restore workflow be sourced and approved?
resolved_ambiguities.decision: Restore requests reference an authoritative backup_run_id, not a raw backend snapshot id. Approval is required unless policy metadata explicitly disables it; adapter execution is gated on approved/not_required durable state.
resolved_ambiguities.evidence: internal/controlplane/backup_restore_handlers.go, internal/service/backup_registry_restore.go, internal/service/backup_restore_coordinator.go, and reactor_backup_requests_test.go verify pending approval prevents executor handoff and approval triggers execution.

resolved_ambiguities.question: How should retention execution state be exposed without a dedicated read-model allocation?
resolved_ambiguities.decision: Retention progress still uses BackupObservation kind 6984 and terminal BackupRetentionResult kind 38414; durable retention run outcomes are also projected through the existing BackupRetentionRegistry 31994, and fleet rollups use BackupRuntimeObservationState 31999.
resolved_ambiguities.evidence: internal/adapters/nostr/projector.go publishes retention run state via KindBackupRetentionRegistry and fleet posture via KindBackupRuntimeObservationState; backup_kinds.go already allocates both kinds.

resolved_ambiguities.question: What is a BackupDefinition in the first domain/repository slice?
resolved_ambiguities.decision: BackupDefinition is the canonical operator-facing registry object that composes repository, policy, recipe, schedule metadata, tenant/environment/owner scope, approval policy, restore target rules, executor targeting fields, labels/grouping, metadata, and audit fields. This slice persists and retrieves the model only; execution semantics are handled by dependent Beads.
resolved_ambiguities.evidence: internal/domain/backup.go, internal/repository/pg_backup_controlplane.go, and internal/db/migrations/000030_backup_definitions.up.sql implement the persisted domain/repository contract.

resolved_ambiguities.question: How should operators see pending restore approval and backup fleet health?
resolved_ambiguities.decision: Restore state carries policy-driven approval_required/approval_requirement plus structured approval reason/audit provenance, while fleet posture is a replaceable runtime observation summarizing queue/running/stale counts, pending approvals, recent outcomes, backend health failures, and failure categories.
resolved_ambiguities.evidence: internal/domain/backup.go, internal/controlplane/backup_restore_handlers.go, internal/service backup coordinators/registry methods, and internal/adapters/nostr/projector.go implement and project these fields.
